exposure: Induction method (Cervical ripening balloon (CRB) vs 10 mg vaginal dinoprostone insert)
cohort: Nulliparous women with a pre-pregnancy body mass index > 30 and singleton-term pregnancies (n = 164, n = 83 CRB group, n = 81 dinoprostone group)
finding: Cervical ripening balloon (CRB) induction was associated with a significantly shorter time to delivery, higher satisfaction, and lower anxiety compared to dinoprostone induction in women with obesity.
mod_finding: While there were no differences in cesarean delivery rates between groups, CRB induction was associated with a significantly lower rate of tachysystole.
